input: read ./prompt.md and follow the instructions there

doc_friction.issue: Item 5 framed the open question as CPU ('time a real STEP in workerd'); the real limit was memory (128 MB isolate), which local workerd does not enforce, so timing in workerd alone would have missed it.

payapps #16 was listed as free and claimed by another run 7 seconds later; with bet #1's only other free item needing a physical Windows PC and Android phone, there was nothing workable on bet #1 this run.

deviations.why: The item asked for a timing; the timing showed the limit is memory, so I also fixed the parser's memory use and added a 6 MB measure cap rather than only replacing the estimate.
deviations.did: parser memory fix (198 -> 132 MB on 12.9 MB file, identical results on 36 files) + MAX_MEASURE_BYTES with a stored reason
deviations.result: tests green; large files now say why instead of failing every Measure click

deviations.why: Bet #1 (payapps) had no workable free item this run, so I took bet #2's only free item.

writeups: docs/posts/2026-11-25-a-step-file-now-sizes-the-blank-in-the-job-shop-quoter.md (extended: 'How big a STEP file it can measure')
notes: Security queue: 0 workable. Ideas inbox empty. Verification: cad-features node --test 75/75; jobshop-quote vitest unit 633/633, worker 282/282; tsc clean (app + cad-features); biome check . clean. Real-file equality: extractFeatures JSON identical old vs new parser on 33 NIST + 3 Onshape STEP files. Timings in workerd 1.20251118.0 (local), heap via Node --max-old-space-size bisection (workerd local does not enforce the 128 MB isolate limit).

pricing.source: Anthropic pricing page (platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing), fetched 2026-11-12. Cache writes are 1.25x input (5-minute) and 2x input (1-hour); cache reads are 0.1x input except 0.05x on Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5 and 0.025x on Fable/Mythos 5.1 and 5.2. Sonnet 5.5 cache_read was 0.20 here until 2026-11-12 (quality audit round 48): records priced before then overstate Sonnet 5.5 cost.

human_equivalent.basis: finding real large STEP files, a workerd bench harness, heap bisection, parser memory fix with equality check, cap + tests + docs: about 1.5 engineer-days

certainty.tokens: high: summed from the per-request `usage` the API returned, as the transcript recorded it, deduplicated by message id
certainty.model: high: the `model` field on each API response, not the configured model
certainty.api_equivalent_usd: medium: measured tokens x list prices in prompts/pricing.json (as_of stated); an equivalent, not a charge: these runs are billed under a subscription
certainty.time: medium: from transcript timestamps; model time is request-to-response, tool time is call-to-result, time waiting on a person is excluded from active time
certainty.human_equivalent: low: the agent's own estimate of how long a competent person would take, with its basis written down; never measured

not_counted: requests the harness makes outside the transcript (context compaction summaries, title generation, safety classifiers), if any
transcripts lost when a cloud session moved to a new container: only files present in this container are read, so a resumed session can undercount
server-tool fees (web search is billed per search, not per token); the count is recorded, not priced
CI minutes and the reviewer bots' own model calls
